subject: Re: Dedicated commit — smoothing above-commit billing and notification cadence
messages:
From: Janelle Ortiz <janelle.ortiz@acme.ai>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, procurement@acme.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated commit — question on above-commit handling

Hi Monica,

We're finalizing the Dedicated commit numbers for Q3 and had one open item from procurement: how Redwood handles short-term bursts above our reserved GPU pool. Specifically: billing cadence (how overage is metered), whether you do any kind of smoothing or credits for transient spikes, and at what point (if any) you throttle versus queue.

We expect occasional spikes when our nightly batch jobs and peak inference coincide — usually 1–6 hours, a few times per month, not sustained. Our procurement team asked whether there's a way to avoid immediate high overage charges for those short bursts.

Can you share a concrete proposal we can put in the SOW (metering window, billing unit, notification cadence, and any optional smoothing/crediting that might be available)? Also send any pricing examples so our finance folks can model scenarios.

Thanks,
Janelle Ortiz
Head of ML Ops
Acme Robotics

Attachments: ACME_RFP_Q3.pdf (pdf)

Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com

Hi Janelle — thanks for laying this out. High level first, then I'll follow with more concrete billing language your legal/procurement can drop into the SOW.

TL;DR proposal: meter and bill in 1-minute GPU-minute increments with a 3-day trailing smoothing window for transient bursts, plus a small one-time smoothing credit pool per month. Throttling only occurs if usage exceeds the commit + smoothing buffer for >24 continuous hours; otherwise requests are served at best-effort. We also provide automated pre-threshold alerts (75%, 90%, 100% of commit + buffer).

Key points:
- Metering unit: GPU-minute (we round up to nearest minute). Billing reported as GPU-hours monthly for clarity.
- Metering window: rolling 60s granularity aggregated to 5-minute and 24-hour views for alerting and invoicing.
- Smoothing: a configurable smoothing credit applied to the invoice that amortizes short spikes over a 72-hour (3-day) lookback; this is intended to avoid one-off large line items for short bursts. Default smoothing pool for your tier: 250 GPU-hours/month (can be traded for a modest discount on committed price).
- Overage rate: standard overage applies when net usage beyond committed + smoothing pool occurs. Our proposed starting overage = committed unit rate * 1.35. If you increase commit within 30 days after a sustained burst, we offer a retroactive partial credit on overage (negotiable).
- Throttling: hard throttle only after 24 continuous hours over commit+buffer. Before that, we maintain service but may shed lower-priority traffic (queueing/backpressure) in extreme contention.

I'll circulate a redlined snippet for SOW language in a follow-up. If this is directionally OK, I can ask Aditya to attach a sample invoice scenario (best, worst, realistic) for your finance team.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: internal: meter/pricing details for ACME proposal

Monica / Laura — adding the technical/pricing specifics we typically include so legal has concrete numbers. These should be treated as negotiable but are what ops and billing can support without special engineering changes.

Metering & billing specifics we recommend for Acme:
- Billing unit: 1 GPU-minute (billed as GPU-minute, shown as GPU-hours on invoice)
- Rounding: round up to the next full minute for each vGPU allocation
- Aggregation windows: 60s raw, aggregated into 5m for telemetry, 24h for 95th-percentile reports (used for trend analysis, not billing)
- Smoothing policy: 72-hour rolling smoothing window. Any minute of usage within the window first consumes smoothing credit, then committed capacity, then overage billing, in that order.
- Smoothing credit pool: default 250 GPU-hours/month. Unused smoothing credits do not roll over. Can be increased in exchange for a 2–4% uplift on committed monthly fee or deeper committed discount (tradeable).
- Overage pricing: baseline formula = committed unit price * 1.35. For customers with a renewal/expansion clause within 30 days, we apply a 10% rebate on billed overage back to the next invoice if commit increased to cover the burst.
- Throttling trigger: if usage > (commit + smoothing pool equivalent) continuously for 24 hours, system switches to degradation mode: new requests are queued up to 120s per request, and lowest-priority routes are shed first. Hard throttle only when queueing exceeds configured backpressure thresholds.

Operational notes:
- Alerts: automatic email and webhook alerts at 75/90/100% of (commit + smoothing pool).
- Metering transparency: daily metering CSV export available; we recommend attaching the metering_spec.md to the SOW.

I'll attach a sample pricing sheet for scenarios.

- Aditya
Senior Pricing Ops
Redwood Inference

Hi Janelle — following up with a concise contract-ready paragraph and a proposed commercial concession we can include in the SOW. See below (you can paste this into the SOW):

---
Dedicated Overage and Smoothing (proposed SOW language):
Redwood will meter Dedicated GPU capacity in one-minute GPU-minute units, aggregated on a rolling 60s basis and reported in 5-minute and 24-hour summaries. For the Term, Customer will receive a Smoothing Credit Pool of 250 GPU-hours per calendar month which will be consumed before overage charges are applied. Overages are billed at the Overage Rate, defined as 135% of the Committed Unit Price. In the event Customer increases their Commitment within 30 days of a sustained burst (>=24 continuous hours over Commit + Smoothing Pool), Redwood will apply a 10% rebate to the overage charges related to that burst back to Customer's next invoice. Redwood will provide automated alerts at 75%, 90%, and 100% of (Commit + Smoothing Pool). Hard throttling will only be enacted after 24 continuous hours of usage above Commit + Smoothing Pool; before that, Redwood will serve requests at best effort and may queue for up to 120 seconds during contention.
---

Commercial concession (proposal):
As a gesture to support Acme's initial ramp, Redwood will apply a one-time Smoothing Bonus of 100 GPU-hours for the first billing cycle (in addition to the standard pool) and a 5% discount on overage rates for any overage event under 48 cumulative hours in the first 90 days after contract signature.

Attached: smoothing_pricing_sheet.xlsx and metering_spec.md with the telemetry fields we export. If that wording looks good, I'll ask Legal to stitch this into the SOW and send a DocuSign SOW for signature.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Monica — this is helpful and much closer to what procurement wanted. A couple quick clarifications before we sign:
1) If we see repeated short bursts (e.g., 2–3 times / week of 2–6 hours) that cumulatively exceed the smoothing pool, does Redwood auto-notify and recommend a commit increase? Is that recommendation included in the remediation/alerting flow?
2) For throttling: when you say "queue up to 120s," does that apply to all endpoints? We have some latency-sensitive routes that cannot be queued. Can we set per-route policies (priority routes that always get best-effort until hard throttle)?

We like the commercial concession (100 GPU-hours; 5% overage discount) — happy to accept that if you can confirm answers to the two bullets. Also please send the DocuSign SOW when ready so procurement can sign.

Thanks,
Janelle

Hi Janelle — looping in legal/ops signoff. Answers inline: 

1) Auto-notify and recommendation: yes — Redwood's billing/ops engine will surface if short bursts are recurrent and will include an automated recommendation to increase commit with an estimated cost delta. Those recommendations will be emailed and available as a prioritized item in the Redwood Console (we'll include the console link in the SOW). This is part of standard account-level telemetry for Dedicated customers.

2) Per-route policy: yes — Dedicated customers can mark routes as "high-priority" in their routing policy. High-priority routes will be served preferentially and are subject to queueing only when the system enters degradation mode; they are the last to be shed. We'll include a short appendix describing per-route priority configuration.

Contract actions: we've updated the SOW language to include the Smoothing Bonus and the 5% overage discount for short events under 48 hours in the first 90 days. DocuSign SOW is attached here: https://docusign.com/rooms/abc123-sow. Procurement, please countersign and return.

I'll also attach the metering CSV schema and an example invoice scenario to the DocuSign package.

Regards,
